The appellants have filed these Misc. Appeals under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the award dated 18.12.2013 passed by the Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28782 2 MA-638-2014 Claim Case No.369/2011.
1.1

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: M.A. No.638/2014 has been filed by the claimant while M.A. No.1026/2014 has been filed by the Insurance Company.
1.2 The Insurance Company has filed the appeal on the ground that the finding regarding permanent disability was erroneous as the treating doctor was not examined.
On the other hand, the claimant contends that the compensation awarded is inadequate.

2. Short facts of the case are that on 04.04.2011 at around 04.13 PM, the appellant was travelling with his friend Lattu as a pillion rider on a motorcycle bearing registration number MP-HBB-3720 Remal Barela vs Mahesh Mandloi on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178724756/
1
en-route to Khargone.

When they reached near Sanchi Milk Dairy on Temla-Khargone road,
respondent No.2 while driving a Mahendra Pickup bearing registration number MP-10-G-0184 in a rash and negligent manner, collided with the motorcycle.
As a result of the accident, the appellant's friend Lattu died and the appellant sustained grievous injuries on various parts of his body.
2.1 The appellant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him.

The Claims Tribunal after considering the evidence available on record, awarded a total compensation of Rs.4,07,200/- out of which amount of Rs.1,72,800/- was awarded towards permanent disability, Rs.2,26,400/-towards medical expenses and Rs.7,000/- for non-pecuniary heads.
3. Learned counsel for the claimant submits that the assessment of income by the Claims Tribunal is not correct.
He further submits that the appellant was earning Rs.9,000/- per month while working as a mason;
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28782 3 MA-638-2014 however, the Claims Tribunal assessed his income on a notional basis at Rs.4,000/- per month, despite treating him as a skilled labourer 3.1
He submits that the appellant sustained permanent disability, which was certified as 50% in the head, 10% in the jaw and 7% in the right palm, amounting to a total of 67% permanent disability.
However, the Claims Tribunal has considered only 20% disability with respect to the whole body.
He further submits that such a reduction in the assessment of permanent disability is neither proper nor justified.
3.2 He submits that the extent of permanent disability was duly proved by examining Dr.Surendra Bapat (AW-3) and by exhibiting the permanent disability certificate (Exh. P-12).
He, therefore, prays for enhancement of compensation by modifying the assessment of permanent disability accordingly.
He also submits that the Tribunal failed to consider future prospects while computing the income of the appellant.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that Dr.Surendra Bapat was not the treating doctor and that the permanent disability certificate, which was exhibited as Exh. P-12 was not issued by a District Medical Board.
Therefore, the Claims Tribunal ought not to have relied upon the same.
He further submits that the compensation awarded on the basis of 20% permanent disability is not sustainable.
Accordingly, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
6.

From perusal of Exh. P-12, it is crystal clear that the certificate NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:28782 4 MA-638-2014 states the appellant has suffered 50% permanent disability in the head, 10% in the jaw and 7% in the right hand.

Accordingly, a total of 67%
permanent disability in different parts of the body has been certified by the doctor who was examined as AW-3.
Although the Claims Tribunal has not disbelieved the said certificate, it has considered the disability as 20% with respect to the whole body.

Remal Barela vs Mahesh Mandloi on 27 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178724756/
2 7.

As regards the contention of the Insurance Company that the said certificate was not issued by the treating doctor, it must be noted that there is no material on record to indicate that the certificate is not genuine.
Furthermore, no infirmity has been demonstrated in the statement of Dr.Surendra Bapat (AW-3), who remained firm during his cross-examination before the Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal regarding permanent disability.
8. However, considering that the appellant was working as a mason and suffered permanent disability to his head and right hand, the disability is assessed at 25%.

9. As regards the income, although the claimant asserted that he was earning Rs.9,000/- per month,
there is not a single piece of material evidence on record to support this claim.
Hence, the Claims Tribunal rightly rejected it.
However, on perusal of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority, it is observed that the minimum wages for a skilled labour as of 04.04 2011 were Rs.4,675/- per month.
Accordingly, this amount is taken as the monthly income of the appellant.

In view of the law laid down by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:28782 5 MA-638-2014 Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 , an addition of 40% is made to the said income, considering that the appellant was 22 years of age at the time of the accident as per para 18 of the award.

sentences.text: 10. After the above modifications, the compensation for permanent disability is assessed at Rs.3,53,430/-.
Accordingly, the total compensation payable to the claimant now comes to Rs.5,87,830/-.

11. In view of the above analysis and conclusions drawn by this Court, the appeal of the Insurance Company i.e. M.A. No.1026/2014 is hereby dismissed and M.A. No.638/2014 filed by the claimant is allowed in part.
12.

The appellant shall be paid an amount of Rs.1,80,630/- (being the differential amount) along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal.
